options.content: **These are live-sampled, reference-free metrics** from `app/eval/jobs/online_eval.py` scoring `ONLINE_EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE` of real traffic with the lexical judge (no ground truth available on live traffic, no GPU judge call — see the module docstring). They are a drift signal, not a substitute for the gated CI gold-set suite (`app/eval/thresholds.yaml`, recall@5/MRR/nDCG/faithfulness-with-ground-truth), which only runs in `eval-gate.yml` against the curated gold set. Both empty/flat panels usually mean `ONLINE_EVAL_ENABLED`/`ONLINE_EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE` are unset (both default off) or `PROMETHEUS_ENABLED` is false.

panels.title: Lexical answer relevancy (rolling, sampled live traffic)
Hallucination flag rate (numeric-grounding check, rolling)
panels.description: 0.72 threshold line matches thresholds.yaml's hallucination.hallucination_rate max (offline gate) — same detector, different traffic sample, so a sustained crossing here is a meaningful early-warning signal.

panels.title: End-to-end stream latency — p50 / p95 (sampled live traffic)
panels.description: 60000ms threshold line matches thresholds.yaml's latency.p95_sec ceiling (offline gate, same production hardware).

panels.title: Samples scored in most recent online_eval run
CI Tier-2 (gated, real judge) — below this line

options.content: **These come from `eval-gate.yml`'s `tier2-full-suite`** — the real Qwen2.5-7B-judge numbers `thresholds.yaml` actually gates on (`retrieval` is enforced; the rest are informational until re-baselined — see the header comment in `thresholds.yaml`), pushed to Prometheus Pushgateway after every post-deploy and manually-dispatched Tier-2 run (not on every PR — Tier-1 has no network path to this box and scores an ephemeral checkout, not the production container; see `.github/workflows/eval-gate.yml`'s comment on the push step). Values persist between runs (Pushgateway semantics) — a flat line between two points is real, not a gap in scraping.

panels.title: Retrieval quality — recall@5 / recall@10 / hit_rate (CI Tier-2, GATED)
panels.description: Gate floors (thresholds.yaml, v5 production baseline): recall@5 >= 0.4835, recall@10 >= 0.5259, hit_rate >= 0.6447. A breach here is what triggers eval-gate.yml's auto-rollback (see docs/runbooks/phase-31-monitoring.md §6) — this panel should visually confirm what the job log already said, not be the first place you learn about it.

panels.title: Retrieval ranking quality — MRR / nDCG@10 / context_precision (CI Tier-2, GATED)
panels.description: Gate floors: MRR >= 0.3380, nDCG@10 >= 0.3823, context_precision >= 0.0255 — context_precision's absolute value is low by design (thresholds.yaml flags it as a known future retrieval-quality target, not a bug in this panel).

panels.title: Generation quality — faithfulness / answer_relevancy / context_recall (CI Tier-2, informational)
panels.description: NOT gated — thresholds.yaml keeps `generation` informational-only pending re-baseline on the current judge (see its header comment). Real judge (Qwen2.5-7B, app/eval/judges/qwen_judge.py), unlike the lexical faithfulness panel above.

panels.title: Hallucination rate — real judge (CI Tier-2, informational)
panels.description: thresholds.yaml gate ceiling: max 0.72 (not currently enforced — hallucination stays informational, only retrieval gates). Compare against the live-sampled panel above: same detector (hallucination_flag_single), different traffic — this is the curated gold set, that one is sampled production traffic.

panels.title: Last Tier-2 push age
panels.description: Yellow past 2 days, red past 7 — Tier-2 only runs post-deploy and (once enabled) nightly, so this is expected to sit in the hours-to-a-day range on an active release cadence, not near-zero like a scrape-based metric.

panels.title: Live Retrieval Quality (online, sampled) — below this line

options.content: **Monitoring Phase 6.** Rolling means from the SAME online_eval.py run as the panels above, over the SAME sampled shadow-collection rows — just aggregating the retrieval fields shadow_sampler.py has stamped on every row since Phase 2 (top1_score/mean_topk_score/retrieval_count) instead of only query/answer/contexts. Complements app/eval/jobs/drift_eval.py's p-values below (a p-value says *did this change*, not *what is it right now* — these two panels are the *now* view).

panels.title: Live top-1 / mean-top-k rerank score (rolling)
panels.description: The same top1_score/mean_topk_score app/eval/jobs/drift_eval.py's QUALITY columns compare reference-vs-current — this is the raw trend, not the statistical-drift verdict. A steady decline here is worth investigating even before it crosses drift_eval's significance threshold.

panels.title: Live retrieval doc count (rolling)
panels.description: Mean number of sources returned per sampled query. A sudden drop toward 0 across many queries usually means retrieval itself is failing (Qdrant/BM25), not that answers got worse — check circuit_breaker_state and monitoring/grafana/dashboards/system_health.json's infra panels first.

options.content: **Monitoring Phase 6.** `agent_controller_*` metrics (app/agents/agent_controller.py) have existed since before this monitoring effort but were never dashboarded. Route distribution itself is already covered by the "Routing decision share" panel above (magik_eval_online_route_share) — this section is latency/errors/fallback/concurrency, the other half of "agent health." There is no "tool calls per request" panel: AgentExecutor.run() is a single classify-and-dispatch, not an iterative tool-chaining loop (see CLAUDE.md's Query/RAG flow section), so that metric does not exist to show — showing one would mean inventing data the architecture doesn't produce.

panels.title: Agent controller latency — p50/p95 by decision
Agent controller errors + fallback rate
panels.description: A fallback invocation is not itself an error (see agent_controller.py's _fallback()) — it's the low-confidence catch-all path. Sustained fallback growth with flat error_type series usually means routing confidence is degrading, not that the agent is crashing.

options.content: **Monitoring Phase 3/6.** app/eval/jobs/drift_eval.py compares a fixed reference-window snapshot (DRIFT_REFERENCE_PATH, built via `python -m app.eval.jobs.drift_eval --build-reference`) against the current sampled-traffic window on 4 columns (query_length/top1_score/mean_topk_score/latency_ms), using a KS-test — NOT Evidently (see that module's docstring for why: every Evidently version pulls in a bundled litestar/uvicorn/plotly web-server stack for what's really a KS-test on 4 columns). Requires DRIFT_ENABLED=true and a built reference — panels below read as zero/empty until both are true. Alerts: magik-drift-warning / magik-drift-critical in monitoring/alerts/rules.yml.

panels.title: Drift dataset score (fraction of columns drifted)
panels.description: Volume of drift alone, NOT severity — a high score here with severity still at Info means several columns moved but no QUALITY column (top1_score/mean_topk_score) moved in the degrading direction. See drift_eval.py's module docstring on why those are classified separately.

panels.title: Drift per-column p-value (lower = more drift)
panels.description: KS-test p-value per tracked column. p < 0.05 (below the red/green threshold line) means that column's current-window distribution is statistically distinguishable from the reference window.

panels.title: Reference / current window size
panels.description: Both read 0 until DRIFT_ENABLED=true, ONLINE_EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE > 0, and a reference file has been built — see the section header above.
